problem_statement.source: Task 00 audit finding, re-confirmed directly for this task by reading ebpf-agent/cmd/agent/main.go before Task 11: the agent watches/lists RuntimeSecurityPolicy objects only. It never imports, watches, or reads AIPlacementDecision (D) at all -- grep for 'AIPlacementDecision' in ebpf-agent/cmd/agent/main.go returned zero matches before this task. It copies p.Spec.Derivation.DecisionHash/PolicyHash (values the OPERATOR itself computed) directly into signed evidence, without ever independently verifying D's Ed25519 signature or recomputing what P should contain.
problem_statement.threat_model_inconsistency: The project's stated threat model (Task 00) treats the Kubernetes control plane as potentially untrusted/compromised. A worker that applies whatever RuntimeSecurityPolicy.Spec it receives, with zero independent check against the signed decision that policy claims to be derived from, gives a compromised or buggy controller (or anyone with RuntimeSecurityPolicy write access) the ability to silently rewrite enforcement rules for any pod -- the worker has no way to detect this before applying it.
problem_statement.before_this_task: Confirmed empirically, not just by code reading: a plain `kubectl patch runtimesecuritypolicy ... --type=merge -p '{"spec":{"exec":{"allowedPaths":["/bin/sh"]}}}'` against the pre-Task-11 agent image was applied by the agent with no rejection of any kind (the same command is what this task's tampered-P test uses, now correctly rejected).

implementation.verify_signature_d: Reuses operator/pkg/token.VerifyForPod (the SAME verification code the operator's own controller calls, not a reimplementation) -- checks Ed25519 signature, expiry, and (when provided) pod UID / node identity binding.
implementation.hash_p_received_vs_hash_derive_d: The agent independently reconstructs the policyHashMaterial the operator's controller would derive from D (mirroring internal/controller/policy_derivation.go, which cannot be imported directly -- separate Go module, internal/ visibility), hashes it (operator/pkg/crypto.CanonicalSHA256Hex), and compares against the same hash computed from the policy's ACTUAL received field values (not a hash-shaped field the same attacker could also have rewritten).
implementation.freshness_version_anti_replay: Freshness/version are checked by VerifyForPod's own token-expiry logic plus a new agent-local ReplayLedger (in-memory; rejects rollback and same-version/different-nonce replay). Honest limitation stated in trustverify.go and exclusions.md: this ledger does not persist across agent restarts, unlike the operator's own ConfigMap-backed decision_ledger.go (not importable from this separate module).
implementation.pod_uid_node_identity: Passed into VerifyForPod from the live pod object / this node's own --node-name, reusing the existing binding-drift check semantics already established in Task 06/07's work.
implementation.on_failure: The agent applies a safe deny-all substitute plan (DefaultAction=deny, empty allow-lists, for Exec/FileAccess/NetworkEgress/DeviceAccess) instead of the received (untrusted) policy content -- 'the worker rejects it' means deny, not silently skipping/leaving the cgroup untracked.

valid_D_correct_P.description: Normal flow: mint a real signed decision, let the operator derive the policy, observe the agent's steady-state verdict.

valid_D_tampered_P.description: After reaching a confirmed-accepted baseline (proving the policy really was trusted before tampering), patch the live RuntimeSecurityPolicy's Exec.AllowedPaths directly (simulating a compromised/buggy control plane rewriting P post-derivation, D unchanged) and observe the agent's verdict on the next reconcile cycle.

verdict_determination: Read directly from the agent's own structured log output (policy=<key> ... reason="..." for rejections, "applied policy" for acceptance), not inferred from side effects alone -- though the tampered-P rejection is ADDITIONALLY confirmed via direct bpftool map dump showing the tampered AllowedPaths entry never reached the kernel's exec_rules map (raw/exec-rules-map-after-tamper.json).
sample_size_discipline: n = number of independent pod/decision/policy triples created and torn down per condition (5 each), never assertions x runs.
